According to the factor theorem, if [MATH: (ax-b)] is a factor of [MATH: p(x),] then the root [MATH: x = \dfrac{b}{a}] is also a root of [MATH: p(x).]

Here, we are considering the factor [MATH: (3x+2).] The root of this factor can be found by setting the factor equal to [MATH: 0] and solving:

[MATH: 3x + 2|= 0; 3x|= − 2; x|= − (2)/(3)]

According to the factor theorem, then, since [MATH: (3x+2)] is a factor of [MATH: p(x),] the root [MATH: x=-\dfrac{2}{3}] is also a root of [MATH: p(x).] This means [MATH: p \left( -\dfrac{2}{3} \right)=0,] so we have

[MATH: \eqalign{ p\left(-\frac23\right) &= 0 \[5pt] 3\left(-\frac23\right)^3-k\left(-\frac23\right)^2+4 &= 0 \[5pt] -\frac89-\frac{4k}{9}+\frac{36}{9} &= 0 \[5pt] -8 - 4k + 36 &= 0 \[5pt] 28 &= 4k \[5pt] k &= 7. }]

Here, we are considering the factors [MATH: (x+1)] and [MATH: (x-3).] The roots of these factors can be found by setting the factors equal to [MATH: 0] and solving:

[MATH: x + 1 = 0|⇒x = − 1; x − 3 = 0|⇒x = 3]

According to the factor theorem, then, since [MATH: (x+1)] and [MATH: (x-3)] are factors of [MATH: p(x),] the roots [MATH: x=-1] and [MATH: x=3] are also roots of [MATH: f(x).] This means [MATH: f(-1)=0] and [MATH: f(3)=0,] so we have

[MATH: f(− 1)|= 0; a(− 1)^{3} + b(− 1)^{2} − 16(− 1) − 15|= 0; − a + b + 1|= 0; a − b|= 1,; f(3)|= 0; a(3)^{3} + b(3)^{2} − 16(3) − 15|= 0; 27a + 9b − 63|= 0; 3a + b|= 7.]

This gives a system of equations

[MATH: {a − b = 1; 3a + b = 7.]

Adding the equations, we eliminate [MATH: b] and get

[MATH: 4a = 8\quad\Rightarrow\quad a=2.]

Finally, substituting [MATH: a=2] in either equation gives [MATH: b=1.] So our solutions are [MATH: a=2] and [MATH: b=1.]

[MATH: x + 1 = 0|⇒x = − 1; x − 3 = 0|⇒x = 3]

According to the factor theorem, then, since [MATH: (x+1)] and [MATH: (x-3)] are factors of [MATH: p(x),] the roots [MATH: x=-1] and [MATH: x=3] are also roots of [MATH: f(x).] This means [MATH: f(-1)=0] and [MATH: f(3)=0,] so we have

[MATH: {a − b = 1; 3a + b = 7.]

[MATH: 4a = 8\quad\Rightarrow\quad a=2.]

Finally, substituting [MATH: a=2] in either equation gives [MATH: b=1.] So our solutions are [MATH: a=2] and [MATH: b=1.]
